title: Anthropic Launches First AI Bug Scanner to Protect Open Source Software
summary:
The AI startup is introducing a free, opt-in tool to help open-source software maintainers identify security flaws and distribute fixes more rapidly via its new Anthropic Cyber Mission. This initiative includes the release of the OSS Scanner, which uses the Claude Mythos model to detect vulnerabilities and provide proofs of concept. As part of the broader mission, the company is also deploying a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program with 11 founding partners, including CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Rockwell Automation, to protect utility and transportation grids.

The security effort expands upon a 3 tier clearance system for Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5, which is available to vetted security professionals for authorized penetration testing and malware analysis. Anthropic accelerated these protections after Project Glasswing partners identified 129,000 verified vulnerabilities, including 33,000 rated as high or critical severity. The startup also noted that rival Zhipu AI's open GLM-5.3 model could generate exploits in 50 of 410 attempts, nearly matching the capabilities of Anthropic's Mythos Preview.

selectedTweets.text:
Through The Mission (launching today), we'll release research, tools, and resources to help secure the world.

Two programs: 1/ OSS Scanner, inspired by OSS Fuzz, for maintainers to receive more bug reports/pocs/fixes faster and 2/ the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, where we will work with critical infrastructure providers to figure out what works then scale them up. Backed by our own research and engineers.

Think of the Mission as the ~complement to our model access. We recently expanded cyber access this wk via our new CVP. But we need to make it really easy to find & fix everything, but also rewrite software/systems, especially for critical infrastructure.

Our sense is we've got a ~few years to transform security. That's going to take require a fast feedback loop that brings AGI cybersecurity research into the world. We've built a very cool team, led by @benhawkes, and then we'll scale our work as we learn what works.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic is opening Claude Mythos 5.1 to vetted cyber defenders through 3 access tiers that absorb Project Glasswing. 

Until now, only Glasswing members got Mythos, while the Cyber Verification Program loosened filters on Opus and Sonnet for vetted security teams. 

Anthropic ran Opus 5.5 through its CyScenarioBench attack scenarios 50 times per tier, and without program access every run stopped at the first prompt. 
anthropic

Claude now gives more hacking help the more Anthropic trusts you and the more dangerous the systems you are allowed to attack.

A hospital security team or a lone researcher gets help analyzing malware and fixing flaws, but Claude won't help them attack anything.

A penetration-testing firm can also have Claude break into client systems it is hired to test, though ransomware stays blocked.

Only organizations vetted with the US government can use Claude to probe power grids, flight systems and interbank networks.

The expansion follows Anthropic's finding that Zhipu AI's freely downloadable GLM-5.3 built working exploits in 50 of 410 attempts, nearly matching Mythos Preview's 56.

Anyone can strip that model's safety refusals, as Anthropic did for about $4,400 of compute, so attackers already have near-Mythos exploit skills and so in many sense withholding Mythos mostly handicaps defenders.

selectedTweets.text:
HOLY. Anthropic is turning access to its strongest cyber capabilities into a 3-tier clearance system.

Defense Access → Red Team Access → Specialized Access.

The higher you go, the fewer cyber blocks. Red Team Opus 5.5 hit 34/50 tasks with ZERO blocks, effectively matching the model with safeguards removed.

Then there’s Mythos.

Claude Mythos 5.1 is the SAME underlying model as generally available Fable 5.1. Mythos just has more permissive safeguards for vetted users.

Why does that matter?

Project Glasswing partners using Mythos found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities.

>33,000+ high/critical
>some would’ve taken months or YEARS to find
>Anthropic says the true impact could be at least 5× higher
